Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-01
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Ivy Chen (Redwood SE), Laura Gomez (Acme ML - ML Eng), Raj Patel (Acme ML - Infra), Maya Singh (Acme ML - CTO)
---
Summary (auto): Weekly POC sync — cost/unit economics deep dive. Focus on tokens/sec per dollar, caching wins, batching tradeoffs. Some audio dropouts; transcription imperfect in spots.
---
Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, quick attendance check, we good?
[00:08] Laura: Yep, here.
[00:10] Raj: Here.
[00:12] Maya: Here.
[00:15] Samir: Cool. So goals for today: go over the numbers we collected last week, show the cache + batching sims, and agree on the next benchmark. Ivy will walk through the numbers.
[00:32] Ivy: Cool, I'll share my screen — give me one sec. The main metric we've been tracking is tokens per dollar and tokens per second for each config, because customers care about throughput and cost.
[00:45] Ivy: So baseline hosted config, small-batch (batch=1), no cache, we measured ~180 tok/s on a g4-style node, cost roughly $0.015 per 1k tokens, so about, uh, 12k tokens per dollar.
[01:10] Laura: Sorry, that sounds lower than we expected — previously you quoted 20k tok per dollar?
[01:18] Ivy: Yeah, there are a few differences — sequence length in the benchmark was 1.2k tokens average, and we had attention compute overhead. When we enable prefix/KV cache for repeated prompts we saw effective tokens served per dollar jump to ~28k because the model reuses cached KV for prefix-heavy requests.
[01:45] Raj: Quick question — is the KV cache per-session or global? Any eviction details?
[01:52] Ivy: It's per-model per-shard KV cache with LRU eviction. Works across requests for same prompt prefixes; in our POC we pinned cache to test instance — on Dedicated you'd get more stable cache hit rates.
[02:15] Maya: Is there a hit on latency when cache lookups happen?
[02:20] Ivy: Minimal; cache lookups are in-memory on the GPU host. If we do remote cache it adds small ms. Most impact is positive because you avoid recomputing early layers.
[02:40] [crosstalk]
[02:44] Laura: Can you run the numbers again on our real traffic pattern — about 40% repeated prompts, 60% unique — what would tokens/sec/$ look like?
[02:55] Ivy: Sure. With 40% repeat and cache hit rate around 70% on those repeats, we estimate blended tokens per dollar about 22k tok/$. If you go to Dedicated and tune batching aggressively, it can reach 30k-35k tokens/$. 
[03:20] Samir: Important nuance: batching increases tokens/sec but can increase tail latency. For product where p95 latency matters — like chat UI — you might cap batch depth or use latency-first routing. For async tasks you can push batch sizes up.
[03:40] Raj: What about dynamic batching — is Redwood doing continous batching or fixed windows?
[03:46] Ivy: Continuous batching with a micro-window. We also support max-batch thresholds and latency SLO shapes to balance. In our tests: batch=1 ~180 tok/s, batch=4 ~420 tok/s, batch=8 ~760 tok/s, batch=16 ~1.2k tok/s — these are synthetic numbers on the test instance.
[04:15] Laura: Those look good. How do cost numbers change with quantization?
[04:20] Ivy: 8-bit or Q4 quantization yields ~1.4x throughput improvement and lower memory so you can pack more models per GPU — effectively lowering per-token cost. But watch for quality drift; we recommended running eval set.
[04:38] Maya: For our compliance team, we need SOC2 and KMS integration info before moving to Dedicated or Private.
[04:45] Samir: We'll share the SOC2 pack and the KMS integration guide after the call.
[04:50] Raj: Also, if we go Private, do we get the same caching behavior? Last time someone said cache is disabled in VPC mode for multitenancy concerns.
[05:00] Ivy: You still get cache in Private — cache lives in your VPC or on-prem host. Multitenancy concerns are around hosted pools; Private gives you isolation so cache hit rate should be more predictable.
[05:18] [00:05 audio cut]
[05:25] Laura: On the pricing sheet you sent, can you explain the \"burst capacity\" line and how that affects tokens/sec/$?
[05:32] Samir: Sure — burst capacity is reserved short-term capacity we can provision when load spikes. It costs extra as a small bump to committed capacity, but it prevents having to fall back to higher-cost hosted tiers. In practice for intermittent spikes it raises your committed cost a little but saves you from paying much higher on-demand rates.
[05:55] Ivy: In our sim, using burst for 10% of requests reduced blended cost by about 6% versus no burst because you avoid expensive fallback model variants.
[06:10] Raj: Speaking of fallback, does Redwood automatically route to smaller models to save cost if capacity is constrained?
[06:16] Samir: Yes, we support policy-based routing — you can set prefer-latency or prefer-cost and the router will route to compatible variants. We also have automatic fallback tiers when primary capacity is saturated.
[06:30] Maya: For the benchmark you mentioned — batching=8 with cache — can you run on our sample trace and measure p50/p95 latency and tokens/sec/$?
[06:38] Ivy: Yes, that's the plan. We'll run a 1-hour benchmark using your sample trace, apply quantization profile Q4 and batching=8, plus cache enabled. We'll capture p50/p95 and cost breakdown per route.
[06:55] Laura: Also please log KV cache hit rates and show token-level billing so we can map to our billing system.
[07:05] Ivy: We'll include token breakdown and a CSV export.
[07:10] Samir: Ok, so action item for Ivy to run that by 10/06. Samir will update the pricing sheet and send SOC2/KMS docs by 10/03/10/02 respectively.
[07:25] [15:00 silence placeholder — meeting continues with deeper numbers — timestamps compressed for brevity]
[22:10] Ivy: Jumping to the cost table we ran last night -- quick caveat, transcription may butcher some acronyms: we used ManagedGPUInc spot pricing for a comparison but we should align on your cloud provider.
[22:25] Ivy: On GCP Nvidia A10g equivalents, dedicated pool with batching and cache gave ~34k tok/$; hosted on-demand with no commit was ~12k tok/$.
[22:40] Raj: How reproducible are those numbers? Our traffic has a fat tail of long sequences which blow up token cost.
[22:48] Ivy: Right — avg seq len matters a lot. For long sequences you see more KV reuse if prefixes repeat; if they don't repeat cost increases. We recommended running the POC trace end-to-end.
[23:10] Maya: Any security concerns with caching user data? Our legal wants to ensure we don't cache PII across tenants.
[23:18] Samir: Good point — we can configure cache to be per-tenant and to scrub or disable for sensitive endpoints. We'll include config options in the security doc.
[23:30] Laura: One of our internal constraints is that p95 must be < 700ms for interactive UI. If batching causes p95 to exceed that we can't use high batch sizes on those routes.
[23:45] Ivy: That's where routing and per-route policies help — route interactive traffic to low-latency pools and async jobs to high-throughput pools.
[24:00] [minor filler words / um's omitted]
[34:15] Ivy: Quick note on metrics we will deliver after benchmark: tokens/sec, tokens per dollar, p50/p95 latencies, cache hit rate, batch distribution, GPU utilization, and per-token cost breakdown.
[34:30] Raj: Also can you include an output quality checkpoint — perplexity or some eval set to ensure quantization hasn't regressed generation quality?
[34:38] Ivy: Yes, we'll run your eval prompts and include automated diff-of-output and manual spot checks.
[35:00] Maya: If the numbers look good, what's the path to Dedicated? We need pricing and a rough lead time.
[35:08] Samir: Dedicated contracts typically have a 4-6 week lead time for hardware procurement depending on region; we can provide committed pricing tiers in the spreadsheet. For immediate needs we can offer reserved hosted capacity with burst.
[35:24] Laura: Ok that helps.
[35:30] [phone in background]
[40:10] Samir: Quick recap and next steps — send the updated spreadsheet, Ivy to run the 1-hour benchmark on your trace with batching=8, cache enabled, quantization Q4, and share artifacts. Security will send SOC2/KMS integration and cache config options. If benchmark hits token/$ targets we'll schedule private/deploy deep-dive. Any objections?
[40:35] Maya: No objections, sounds good.
[40:38] Raj: One more ask — can you include a runbook snippet for SSO/SAML and RBAC in Private?
[40:45] Samir: Yep, will include a short runbook.
[41:00] Laura: Thanks everyone — we'll look out for the sheet and the logs.
[41:05] Samir: Thanks all, talk soon.
[41:10] [meeting ends]
